05-01.s: Spanish neuroscientist Santiago Ramón y Cajal was born in Petilla de Aragón. He established the neuron doctrine and won the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his foundational work on the structure of the nervous system.

05-01.t: Establishment of Armed Forces Medical College (AFMC), Pune
05-01.s: Armed Forces Medical College was established in Pune on the recommendation of the B. C. Roy Committee by amalgamating Indian Army Medical Corps units into a postgraduate teaching institution.

05-01.t: India Expands COVID-19 Vaccination to All Adults (18+)
05-01.s: India opened Phase 3 of its national COVID-19 vaccination drive to all eligible adults aged 18 and above, alongside the arrival of the first consignment of Sputnik V vaccines.

05-01.t: FDA Launches Medical Device Cybersecurity Program
05-01.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration launched its medical device cybersecurity program to address cybersecurity vulnerabilities and respond to incidents affecting connected clinical devices.

05-02.s: Canadian physician Emily Stowe, the first female doctor to practice in Canada and a pioneer in women's medical education, was born.
Russian pediatrician Nil Fyodorovich Filatov was born. He described infectious mononucleosis (Filatov disease) in 1887 and Filatov-Dukes disease.

05-02.t: Birth of Clinical Scientist Dr. Soumya Swaminathan
05-02.s: Pediatrician and tuberculosis/HIV researcher Dr. Soumya Swaminathan was born in Chennai. She served as Director General of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and later became the Chief Scientist of the World Health Organization.

05-03.t: First North American Medical School Established
05-03.s: The first medical school in North America was established at the College of Philadelphia, laying the foundation for formal medical education in the United States.

05-03.t: Establishment of Central Research Institute (CRI), Kasauli
05-03.s: The Central Research Institute was established in Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh as a premier national centre for medical research, antisera, and vaccine manufacturing including DTP and tetanus toxoid.

05-03.t: Howard T. Ricketts Dies of Typhus
05-03.s: American pathologist Howard Taylor Ricketts, who researched the transmission and causative agents of typhus and Rocky Mountain spotted fever, died of typhus at age 39.

05-04.s: Swiss surgeon Fritz de Quervain was born. He described de Quervain tenosynovitis in 1894 and subacute granulomatous thyroiditis (de Quervain thyroiditis).
English neurologist Sir William Richard Gowers, who described Gowers' sign in 1879 and coined numerous foundational neurological terms, died.

05-05.s: The U.S. Congress passed the Indian Vaccination Act of 1832, appropriating $12,000 to vaccinate Native American populations against smallpox.
Japanese physician Hakaru Hashimoto was born. In 1912, he published the first description of autoimmune chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis, now known as Hashimoto's thyroiditis.

05-05.t: WHO Declares India Free of Yaws
05-05.s: Based on the International Verification Team's recommendations, the WHO Director-General formally declared India free of yaws in Geneva, making India the first country in the world to achieve WHO-certified yaws elimination.

05-06.s: German-born American physician Abraham Jacobi, widely regarded as the "Father of American Pediatrics," was born.
American pharmacologist John Jacob Abel presented his research on an adrenal extract pressor to the Association of American Physicians, naming the active principle "Epinephrin."

05-06.t: Passing of Kala-azar Pioneer Dr. Mohan Mishra
05-06.s: Padma Shri physician Dr. Mohan Mishra passed away at age 83. He was renowned for his pioneering clinical work demonstrating the efficacy of Amphotericin B in treating visceral leishmaniasis (Kala-azar) in India.

05-07.s: Dr. B. Bonardi in Lugano performed the first successful lateralised pubiotomy on a living patient using Leonardo Gigli's newly designed wire saw.

05-08.t: Henrik Sjögren Defends Thesis on Keratoconjunctivitis Sicca
05-08.s: Swedish ophthalmologist Henrik Sjögren defended his doctoral thesis using Rose Bengal to characterize keratoconjunctivitis sicca, linking it to the systemic disorder later named Sjögren syndrome.

05-08.t: Birth of Cardiac Surgeon Dr. Devi Shetty
05-08.s: Padma Bhushan cardiac surgeon Dr. Devi Prasad Shetty was born in Kinnigoli, Karnataka. Founder of Narayana Health, he has performed over 15,000 heart operations and pioneered high-volume, affordable cardiac surgery in India.
The World Health Assembly accepted the WHO Global Commission's recommendation and officially declared the world free of smallpox, making it the first human disease eradicated by vaccination.

05-09.t: First Eye Bank Opens in New York City
05-09.s: The first eye bank dedicated to storing donated corneas for transplantation and ophthalmic research opened in New York City.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Enovid-10 as the world's first commercially produced oral contraceptive pill.

05-10.s: Irish-British surgeon Arthur Edward James Barker, a pioneer of surgical asepsis, local infiltration, and spinal analgesia, was born.

05-10.t: FDA Authorizes Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for Adolescents
05-10.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration authorized the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine for adolescents aged 12 to 15.

05-11.s: Swedish orthopaedic surgeon Erik Sophus von Rosen was born. He developed the von Rosen splint and co-developed the Andrén-von Rosen radiographic view for neonatal hip dislocation.
German ophthalmologist Bernhard Kayser, who co-described the Kayser-Fleischer corneal ring in 1902 as a diagnostic sign of Wilson's disease, died.

05-12.s: The International Council of Nurses officially established May 12, Florence Nightingale's birthday, as International Nurses Day to recognize the contributions of nurses worldwide.

05-12.t: WHO Ends Mpox Public Health Emergency
05-12.s: The World Health Organization declared that the global mpox outbreak no longer constituted a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.

05-13.t: Birth of Malaria Nobel Laureate Sir Ronald Ross in Almora
05-13.s: Sir Ronald Ross was born in Almora in British India. Serving for 25 years in the Indian Medical Service, he proved in 1897 that mosquitoes transmit the malaria parasite, earning the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
Greek-American cytopathologist Georgios Nikolaou Papanicolaou, inventor of the Pap smear for early detection of cervical cancer, was born.

05-14.t: Edward Jenner Administers First Smallpox Vaccination
05-14.s: English physician Edward Jenner inoculated eight-year-old James Phipps with matter from a cowpox lesion on milkmaid Sarah Nelmes, demonstrating protective immunity against smallpox.
German surgeon and pathologist Karl Maximilian Wilhelm "Max" Wilms, who described pediatric nephroblastoma (Wilms' tumor), died.

05-15.s: Hungarian obstetrician Ignaz Semmelweis publicly announced his landmark medical discovery demonstrating that physician handwashing drastically reduced fatal puerperal fever.

05-15.t: WHO Declares India Free of Maternal and Neonatal Tetanus
05-15.s: Following nationwide validation surveys across all 675 districts, the World Health Organization declared India to have achieved Maternal and Neonatal Tetanus Elimination (MNTE), reducing incidence to fewer than one case per 1,000 live births.
The U.S. government officially announced Operation Warp Speed, a public-private partnership coordinating federal agencies and industry to accelerate COVID-19 vaccine and therapeutic development.

05-16.s: Bayer registered "Heroin" as a trademark for diacetylmorphine, initially marketing it internationally as a cough suppressant before halting production in 1913 due to widespread addiction.

05-16.t: Jonas Salk Vaccinates His Family Against Polio
05-16.s: Virologist Jonas Salk administered his experimental inactivated polio vaccine to his wife and three sons during early safety testing prior to mass trials.

05-17.s: British physician Edward Jenner, who pioneered smallpox vaccination and established the foundation of immunology, was born in Berkeley, Gloucestershire.
English physician William Heberden the Elder, who described Heberden's nodes and provided the first detailed clinical account of angina pectoris, died.

05-17.t: Passing of Cardiologist and IMA Leader Dr. K. K. Aggarwal
05-17.s: Padma Shri and Dr. B. C. Roy Awardee cardiologist Dr. Krishan Kumar Aggarwal passed away from COVID-19 in New Delhi. A former National President of the Indian Medical Association, he was widely known for public health education and CPR training.

05-18.s: American biochemist Vincent du Vigneaud was born. He is renowned for the isolation, structural identification, and total synthesis of the neuropeptide oxytocin.
British pathologist Michael A. Epstein, co-discoverer of the Epstein-Barr virus and a pioneer in viral cancer research, was born.

05-18.t: Enactment of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA)
05-18.s: India enacted the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), 2003, prohibiting tobacco advertising and regulating the trade, supply, and distribution of tobacco products nationwide.

05-18.t: India's First Uterus Transplant Performed in Pune
05-18.s: Dr. Shailesh Puntambekar and his surgical team at Galaxy Care Hospital in Pune performed India's first uterine transplant, transplanting a mother's womb into her daughter using laparoscopic retrieval.

05-19.t: Louis Pasteur Announces Rabies Vaccine Success in Dogs
05-19.s: French microbiologist Louis Pasteur announced successful immunization of dogs using an attenuated rabies virus, paving the way for the first human rabies vaccination.
German physician Heinrich Irenaeus Quincke, who introduced the lumbar puncture (Quincke's puncture) and described Quincke's pulse and Quincke's edema, died.

05-19.t: Birth of Kala-azar Researcher Dr. Mohan Mishra
05-19.s: Indian physician Dr. Mohan Mishra was born on this day. His clinical trials with Amphotericin B provided a breakthrough cure for drug-resistant visceral leishmaniasis (Kala-azar) in Bihar and eastern India.

05-20.t: James Lind Begins Landmark Scurvy Clinical Trial
05-20.s: British Royal Navy surgeon James Lind began a controlled dietary trial aboard HMS Salisbury demonstrating that citrus fruits cured scurvy, an event celebrated annually as Clinical Trials Day.
American radiologist Henry Khunrath Pancoast, who described superior sulcus lung tumors (Pancoast tumors) in 1924, died.

05-20.t: India Receives WHO Certification for Trachoma Elimination
05-20.s: India formally received the World Health Organization certification for eliminating trachoma as a public health problem, following decades of sustained eye health interventions under the SAFE strategy.

05-21.s: Dutch physician and physiologist Willem Einthoven, who built the first practical electrocardiogram (ECG) in 1903 and defined Einthoven's triangle, was born.

05-21.t: First Known Human Case of H5N1 Avian Influenza
05-21.s: A previously healthy 3-year-old boy in Hong Kong died of viral pneumonia from Influenza A(H5N1), marking the first known human case of H5N1 avian influenza.

05-22.s: German ophthalmologist Albrecht von Gräfe, a founding figure of modern clinical ophthalmology and surgical treatment of glaucoma, was born.

05-22.t: "Jimmy" Radio Broadcast Launches Pediatric Cancer Fundraising
05-22.s: Twelve-year-old cancer patient Einar Gustafson, treated by Sidney Farber in Boston under the pseudonym "Jimmy," was featured on national radio, catalyzing the Jimmy Fund for cancer research.

05-22.t: Passing of Cardiac Surgeon Dr. Nitu Mandke
05-22.s: Pioneering Mumbai cardiac surgeon Dr. Nityanand Mandke passed away at age 55. Trained under Dr. P. K. Sen, he performed over 10,000 cardiac surgeries, mentored surgeons in off-pump techniques, and initiated the hospital project now known as Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital.

05-23.t: Robert James Graves Publishes Description of Graves' Disease
05-23.s: Irish physician Robert James Graves published his clinical lectures in the London Medical and Surgical Journal describing three women with palpitations, goitre, and ocular changes.

05-23.t: FDA Publishes "4-Inch Turtle Rule" Against Salmonellosis
05-23.s: The U.S. FDA banned the commercial sale of live turtles under four inches in carapace length, an intervention estimated to prevent over 100,000 pediatric salmonellosis cases annually.

05-24.s: Physicist and engineer Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit, inventor of the mercury thermometer and the Fahrenheit temperature scale, was born.
German surgeon Friedrich Trendelenburg, who described the Trendelenburg position and Trendelenburg tests for varicose veins and hip abductors, was born.

05-24.t: Birth of Cardiac Surgeon and Innovator Dr. M. S. Valiathan
05-24.s: Dr. Marthanda Varma Sankaran Valiathan was born in Mavelikara, Travancore. A Padma Vibhushan cardiac surgeon and former Director of SCTIMST, he spearheaded the development of India's indigenous Chitra heart valve and promoted Ayurvedic biology.

05-24.t: Passing of CMC Vellore Founder Dr. Ida S. Scudder
05-24.s: Medical missionary Dr. Ida Sophia Scudder passed away at age 89 in Kodaikanal. She founded the Christian Medical College & Hospital in Vellore in 1918 as a medical school for women, growing it into one of India's foremost medical institutions.

05-25.s: The ship Grand-Saint Antoine arrived in Marseille, sparking Europe's last major outbreak of bubonic plague, which killed around 100,000 people.
French neurologist Jean Alexandre Barré, who helped identify Guillain-Barré-Strohl syndrome, was born in Nantes, France.

05-25.t: India Crosses 200 Million COVID-19 Vaccine Doses
05-25.s: India surpassed 200 million cumulative COVID-19 vaccine doses administered nationwide during the expanded adult immunization campaign.

05-26.s: French physician and hematologist Jean Bernard, director of the Institute for Leukemia at the University of Paris and researcher of Hodgkin's disease treatments, was born.

05-26.t: WHO Confirms Ebola Reaches Sierra Leone
05-26.s: The World Health Organization confirmed that the West African Ebola outbreak had spread to Sierra Leone.

05-27.s: Dutch ophthalmologist Franciscus Cornelis Donders, who formulated Donders' Law, the Donders subtraction method in mental chronometry, and invented the ophthalmotrope, was born.
French urologist Fernand Léon Cathelin, who described caudal epidural anesthesia (Cathelin's method) in 1901, was born.

05-28.s: German physician Adolph Kussmaul, who described Kussmaul respiration in metabolic acidosis, Kussmaul's sign, and polyarteritis nodosa, died.

05-28.t: Dionne Quintuplets Born and Survive Infancy
05-28.s: The Dionne quintuplets were born prematurely in Corbeil, Ontario, becoming the first known quintuplets to survive infancy through incubator care and specialist medical support.

05-28.t: Passing of Pathologist & Nutrition Scientist Dr. Vulimiri Ramalingaswami
05-28.s: Padma Vibhushan pathologist Dr. Vulimiri Ramalingaswami passed away at age 79. A former Director of AIIMS New Delhi and Director General of ICMR, his pioneering research on protein-energy malnutrition and iodine deficiency earned global acclaim.

05-29.t: First Mastectomy in North America Performed
05-29.s: Royal physician Michel Sarrazin performed the first documented mastectomy in North America at Hôtel-Dieu de Québec on Sister Marie Barbier de l'Assomption.
Scottish physician and medical scientist Sir Douglas Black, who played a key role in the development of the UK National Health Service, was born.

05-29.t: Passing of Dr. T. M. A. Pai
05-29.s: Dr. Tonse Madhava Ananth Pai, founder of Kasturba Medical College and architect of the Manipal university town, passed away in Manipal at age 81.

05-29.t: Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 Comes into Force
05-29.s: India's Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 officially came into force nationwide, mandating parity between mental and physical health insurance and establishing Mental Health Review Boards.

05-30.s: French physician Ernest Duchesne, who observed in 1897 that certain molds could kill bacteria, anticipating penicillin and antibiotic therapy, was born.
American biochemist Julius Axelrod, who shared the 1970 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his discoveries on neurotransmitter release and reuptake, was born.

05-31.t: WHO Formalizes World No Tobacco Day
05-31.s: World Health Organization member states formalized May 31 as the annual World No Tobacco Day to highlight the preventable burden of tobacco-related disease and death.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Pfizer's Abrysvo vaccine for preventing lower respiratory tract disease caused by RSV in adults aged 60 and older.
